title: What remainders do the sum and take away leave in sevens?
description: Two numbers leave remainders three and five on division by seven. The video writes each as seven times its rows plus its remainder, finds the remainders of the sum and the take away without calculating, shows them with rows of dots, and then checks.
teaching_notes: One idea: add or take away the rows and the remainders separately, and regroup extra loose dots into a row. Watch for students who add the remainders and stop at eight on division by seven.

source: Figure it Out (multiples and remainders, question 7)
video_script.why: The student can find the remainder of a sum and a take away from rows and loose dots for small numbers and now does it for large numbers without calculating.
video_script.substitution: Write each number as seven times its rows plus its remainder, add and take away the rows and the loose parts separately, then check with the real numbers.
video_script.anchor: dots laid in rows of seven, with the loose dots beside the full rows, as in the book's pictures of remainders
video_script.payoff_line: The sum leaves remainder one and the take away leaves remainder two

final_answer.spoken: remainder one for the sum and remainder two for the take away

video_script.design: Two piles of dots in rows of seven. The rows join or come off, the loose dots join or come off, and eight loose dots make one more row with one left.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='first'/>On division by seven, six hundred sixty one leaves remainder three.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Four thousand seven hundred seventy nine leaves remainder five.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Without calculating, what remainders do their sum and their take away leave on division by seven?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: two piles of dots, each in full rows of seven: one with 3 dots loose, the other with 5 dots loose

marks.same: the words the same way as the example in your book appear
marks.rows: each pile is shown as full rows of seven with some dots loose
marks.loose: the loose dots are lit: three on the first pile, five on the second

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>We solve this the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='rows'/>Each number is full rows of seven, with some dots loose.
<bookmark mark='loose'/>Six hundred sixty one has three loose dots, and four thousand seven hundred seventy nine has five.

beats.on_screen: Given: 661 leaves remainder 3 and 4779 leaves remainder 5 on division by 7

marks.given: the first number and its remainder are written
marks.second: the second number and its remainder are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, six hundred sixty one leaves remainder three on division by seven.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Four thousand seven hundred seventy nine leaves remainder five.

beats.on_screen: To find: the remainders of 4779 + 661 and 4779 - 661 on division by 7, without calculating

marks.find: the two things to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the remainders of their sum and take away, without calculating.

marks.write: each number is written as seven times its rows plus its remainder
marks.m: the first number becomes seven m plus three
marks.n: the second number becomes seven n plus five

narration: <bookmark mark='write'/>Step one, write each number as seven times its rows, plus its remainder.
<bookmark mark='m'/>Six hundred sixty one is seven m plus three.
<bookmark mark='n'/>Four thousand seven hundred seventy nine is seven n plus five.

marks.sum: the two numbers are added: the rows join and the loose parts join
marks.eight: eight loose dots fill one more row of seven, with one dot left

narration: <bookmark mark='sum'/>Step two, add them. The rows give seven times m plus n, and the loose parts give eight.
<bookmark mark='eight'/>Eight loose dots fill one more row of seven, with one dot left.
<bookmark mark='rem'/>The remainder of the sum is one.

marks.take: the smaller number is taken from the larger: rows from rows, loose dots from loose dots
marks.loose: three loose dots are taken from five, leaving two

narration: <bookmark mark='take'/>Step three, take the smaller number away from the larger.
The rows give seven times n minus m.
<bookmark mark='loose'/>The loose parts give five take away three, which is two.
<bookmark mark='rem'/>The remainder of the take away is two.

marks.sum: the sum is split into seven hundred seventy seven rows of seven and one over
marks.take: the take away is split into five hundred eighty eight rows of seven and two over

narration: <bookmark mark='sum'/>Step four, check by calculating. The sum is five thousand four hundred forty, which is seven times seven hundred seventy seven plus one.
<bookmark mark='take'/>The take away is four thousand one hundred eighteen.
That is seven times five hundred eighty eight plus two.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The sum leaves remainder one and the take away leaves remainder two.
